label.en: ▲ EST II Math Traps & Pitfalls — Composite, Inverse & Logarithmic Functions

body.en:
• Domain of Composite Functions: For \((f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))\), \(x\) must reside in the domain of \(g\) AND \(g(x)\) must fall within the domain of \(f\). Never simplify algebraically before checking initial domain constraints.
  • Inverse Functions and One-to-One: \(f^{-1}(x)\) exists only if \(f\) passes the Horizontal Line Test. When swapping \(x\) and \(y\), remember that the range of \(f\) becomes the domain of \(f^{-1}\). For restricted domains like \(f(x) = x^2, x \ge 0\), the inverse is \(f^{-1}(x) = \sqrt{x}, x \ge 0\).
  • Logarithm Laws vs. False Analogies: \(\log(a + b) \neq \log a + \log b\). Only multiplication inside yields addition outside: \(\log(ab) = \log a + \log b\). Similarly, \(\frac{\log a}{\log b} \neq \log(a - b)\) — it is the change-of-base formula \(\log_b a\).
  • Function Transformations Order: For \(y = a f(b(x - c)) + d\), horizontal stretch/compression by \(1/|b|\) and shift by \(c\) occur inside, while vertical stretch by \(a\) and vertical shift by \(d\) occur outside. \(f(x - c)\) shifts right by \(c\); \(f(x + c)\) shifts left.

question.en: Given \(f(x) = e^x\) and \(g(x) = \ln(x+1)\), find the domain of \(g(f(x))\) and simplify.

solution.en: \(g(f(x)) = \ln(e^x+1)\). Since \(e^x > 0\) for all \(x\), \(e^x+1 > 1 > 0\). Domain: all reals. Cannot simplify further.

question.en: Let \(f(x) = \dfrac{2x + 1}{x - 3}\) for \(x \neq 3\). (a) Determine the inverse function \(f^{-1}(x)\). (b) State the domain and range of \(f^{-1}(x)\).

solution.en:
(a) Find the inverse function: Set \(y = \dfrac{2x + 1}{x - 3}\). Swap \(x\) and \(y\): \[ x = \dfrac{2y + 1}{y - 3} \implies x(y - 3) = 2y + 1 \implies xy - 3x = 2y + 1. \] Group \(y\) terms: \[ xy - 2y = 3x + 1 \implies y(x - 2) = 3x + 1 \implies f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{3x + 1}{x - 2}. \]

(b) Domain and Range: The denominator of \(f^{-1}(x)\) cannot be zero, so the domain is \((-\infty, 2) \cup (2, \infty)\) or \(x \neq 2\). The range of \(f^{-1}\) equals the domain of \(f\), which is \((-\infty, 3) \cup (3, \infty)\) or \(y \neq 3\).
